subject: MedTech: Sandboxed runtime interop & KMS synchronization — clarifications
messages:
From: Jane Roberts <jane.roberts@medtechinc.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Kevin Li <kevin.li@securecloud.io>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: RFI follow-up: sandboxed runtime interop / KMS sync

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement pack I have a short matrix (attached) with a few deeper clarifications from our security team around private deployments: specifically around
- KMS synchronization across an isolated VPC and our on-prem HSMs,
- ability to use third-party HSMs (PKCS#11 or KMIP),
- operator-driven offline key rotation (procedural acceptance criteria), and
- a short example runbook that shows operator tasks during a patch/upgrade in an air-gapped site.

Can you confirm whether Redwood supports:
1) Key wrapping with external KMS/HSM and the exact transport used for sync (HTTPS pull, push-based replication, KMIP session, etc.)?
2) How you attest that a key fetched into the runtime is not exfiltrated (audit logs, signed manifests)?
3) Whether we can bring our own HSM (Thales/Utimaco) and what integration modes you support?

I've attached the matrix (medtech_rfi_matrix.xlsx) and our security QnA (medtech_security_qna.docx). If you can provide a short excerpt of your operator runbook and any notes on KMS integration, that would be perfect. Ideally we'd have something in the next 48 hours ahead of an internal architecture review.

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Roberts

MedTech Inc.

Subject: Re: RFI follow-up: sandboxed runtime interop / KMS sync

Hi Jane —

Thanks for the matrix and the Q&A. Quick summary up front: Redwood Private supports both cloud KMS connectors and direct HSM integration, we provide auditable key import/unwrap flows with signed manifests and we can operate in an air-gapped site with operator-driven key rotation. I've attached a short runbook excerpt and a tech note that speaks to HSM integration modes.

High-level answers to your numbered items:
1) Key transport: Redwood can operate in several modes depending on customer preference — KMIP over TLS to a reachable HSM (for VPC-connected customers), PKCS#11 via a local connector on the operator-hosted appliance, or a key-wrapping model where the customer's KMS exports wrapped DEKs (data encryption keys) which are then imported into the runtime. For air-gapped sites the common pattern is a signed-wrapped-key bundle transferred over a secure operator channel (SCP/USB with signed manifests).
2) Attestation & non-exfiltration: We provide immutable audit logs for key lifecycle events (import, rotate, delete) and an HMAC-signed manifest that the runtime validates before using imported keys. Audit records include operator identity, timestamp, and a hash of the wrapped-key bundle.
3) BYO-HSM: Yes — we support KMIP and PKCS#11 integrations; common partners include Thales, Utimaco, and Azure Dedicated HSM. The integration note I've attached lists supported versions and recommended connector configuration.

Ben/Marissa — looping you in to confirm a couple of procedural items and to propose a short 45-minute call to walk the MedTech infra team through the runbook excerpt.

Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Hi Jane —

Thanks for the follow-ups. Quick answers inline and I've pasted a sanitized log example below. I'll also bring our security engineer on the call to go deeper. Proposed times: 2026-11-30 09:00 PT or 2026-11-30 11:30 PT — which works for your team?

Signature algorithm and retention:
- We sign wrapped-key bundles using RSA-PSS with SHA-256 by default; customers can opt for ECDSA P-256 if preferred. Redwood does not retain plaintext DEKs or unwrapped key material. We retain the signed metadata (manifest) and audit hashes only — these are one-way and insufficient to recover keys.

KMIP & mTLS:
- Yes, we support KMIP sessions with client-certificate mutual TLS. We also support IP allowlists and mutual-authenticating TLS for connector endpoints.

Sanitized audit log example (single line JSON for ingestion — time and fields redacted):
{ "event": "key_import", "actor": "operator:alice_ops", "method": "wrapped_bundle", "bundle_hash": "sha256:3a7f...b1c9", "manifest_signature": "rsa-pss:base64...", "target_runtime": "private-runtime-1", "timestamp": "2026-11-29T14:58:22Z" }

Attachments: runbook_excerpt.pdf (operator task sequence), kms_integration_notes.md (connector configs).

Ben Carter
Lead, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
